summary.text: Sanford Bishop Jr. is the Democratic incumbent in Georgia's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 1993. A lawyer and Army veteran, he served in both chambers of the Georgia legislature before his election to Congress in 1992. He is the Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies and is seeking re-election.

paragraphs.text: Born February 4, 1947, in Mobile, Alabama, the son of the first president of Bishop State Community College and a librarian.
Graduated from Morehouse College in 1968 and earned a law degree from Emory University School of Law in 1971.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army in 1969, completed basic training at Fort Moore, Georgia, and received an honorable discharge in 1971 after Advanced ROTC training.
Lived in Columbus, Georgia, from 1972 to 1996 and was the primary partner in the law firm Bishop and Buckner, P.C.
Served in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1977 to 1990 and in the Georgia Senate from 1991 to 1992, according to his official biography.
First elected to the U.S. House in 1992 and has served since 1993; his official biography says he is serving his seventeenth term.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, as Ranking Member of its Agriculture, Rural Development, FDA and Related Agencies Subcommittee and a member of the Financial Services and General Government and Military Construction, Veterans Affairs subcommittees; before 2003 he served on the Agriculture, Veterans' Affairs, Post Office and Civil Service, and Intelligence committees.
Was a Senior Democratic Whip in the 112th and 113th Congresses; Georgia Trend magazine has named him among the 100 Most Influential Georgians several times.
According to his official biography, he is married to Vivian Creighton Bishop, has a daughter and a granddaughter, lives in Albany, Georgia, and is a deacon and trustee of Mount Zion Baptist Church.
